context_summary: Irbid is mentioned as a general geographical reference near Khrbet Zeragun.
The page features a schematic drawing of the water tunnels and the site of Khrbet Zeragun.
Wadi Shalalh is mentioned in relation to the water system of Khrbet Zeragun, where the entrance to the water system is accessed from the wadi.
A schematic drawing illustrates the water tunnels at Khrbet Zeragun, detailing their structure, length, and function, including main tunnels, ventilation tunnels, and blocked sections.
The page presents photographs of tunnel sections and blocked tunnels at Khrbet Zeragun.
Photographs show two sections of tunnels and blocked tunnels at Khrbet Zeragun, some constructed and some filled with earth.
The page displays plans of the site of Tepe Gawra, specifically showing Layer VIII and Layer VI, which include a well.
Plans of Tepe Gawra show the location and design of a well within Layer VIII and Layer VI of the site.
The page discusses Early Bronze Age sites in the Negev Highlands and their distribution based on distance from water sources.
The page presents a plan of the site of Ai, showing the location of a storage pool, and a photograph of the pool itself.
A plan of Ai indicates the location of a storage pool within the site, and a photograph provides a visual of this pool.
The page features plans and a reconstruction of the Early Canaanite city of Arad, including its Early Bronze Age city and Iron Age II fortress mound.
Tel Ha-Miẓudot, dating to Iron Age II, is mentioned as a feature within or associated with the plans of Arad.
The page shows a plan of structures surrounding the water pool at Arad.
A plan illustrates the buildings surrounding the water pool at Arad, indicating its central role in the settlement.
The page presents a plan and a reconstructed perspective view of the town of Jawa.
Wadi Rajil is depicted on the plan of Jawa as a revetted water course, indicating its importance to the town's water supply.
The page shows the location of natural pools within Jawa and a schematic plan of Jawa's water systems.
Wadi Rajil is shown on plans illustrating the natural pools and the overall water systems of Jawa.
A plan illustrates the location of natural pools at Jawa, which are integral to the site's water management system.
A schematic plan details the various components of Jawa's water systems, including conduits, pools, and deflection areas.
